Mutational covariance

Source: R/accessors.R
mutational_covariance.Rd

Effects of new mutations on genotypic values in the current population. Genomes are drawn at random (with replacement), and each receives exactly one mutation event of the model's mutation process, at a site chosen in proportion to the mutation rates; the effect is the change in its genotypic value. With epistasis (multilinear()) or binary_b() the effects depend on the genetic background, so the mutational covariance evolves.

Usage

mutational_covariance(pop, n = 10000, effects = FALSE)

Arguments

pop

an evomod_population.

n

number of mutations sampled.

effects

if TRUE, also return the sampled effects.

Value

A list with

  • mean: mean effect of a mutation on each trait (non-zero with directional epistasis);

  • per_mutation: covariance matrix of the effects of one mutation;

  • expected_mutations: expected number of mutation events per genome per generation;

  • M: mutational (co)variance input per generation, expected_mutations * E[dx dx'];

  • effects: the sampled effects (traits x n), if requested.

Examples

model <- evomod_model(additive(loci = 20, traits = 2),
                      mutation(rate = 0.01, cov = 0.1), init_sd = 0.1)
pop <- evolve(model, stabilizing(20, omega = 10), n = 100, seed = 1)
mutational_covariance(pop, n = 5000)
#> $mean
#>        trait1        trait2 
#>  0.0008153449 -0.0021901519 
#> 
#> $per_mutation
#>              trait1       trait2
#> trait1 9.639040e-03 5.277904e-05
#> trait2 5.277904e-05 1.007471e-02
#> 
#> $expected_mutations
#> [1] 0.4
#> 
#> $M
#>              trait1       trait2
#> trait1 0.0038551108 0.0000203931
#> trait2 0.0000203931 0.0040309950
#>
